subject.title: browser tool: include current page URL in before_tool_call params for act/type actions

question: Should OpenClaw expose a policy-checked current browser tab URL to `before_tool_call` handlers for browser `act`/`type`, and should that be hook-param enrichment or a query/context helper?
rationale: This changes a plugin-facing browser security boundary used for credential domain pinning, so automation should not choose the permanent API shape or redaction semantics without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add Hook-Time URL Contract
options.body: Expose an additive, policy-checked current URL for browser `act` and `type` before hooks decide whether to rewrite, approve, or block the call.

options.title: Expose Query Helper
options.body: Keep hook params unchanged and add a supported hook context/query helper that plugins can call when they need the active browser URL.

options.title: Keep Plugin Workarounds
options.body: Leave URL caching and fail-secure cold-cache behavior to credential plugins, accepting duplicated complexity and restart limitations.

recommendation.title: Add Hook-Time URL Contract
recommendation.body: Expose an additive, policy-checked current URL for browser `act` and `type` before hooks decide whether to rewrite, approve, or block the call.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on safe browser URL responses and adjacent browser route policy surfaces.
